passages.text: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and also to the remnant of the people. Ask them, ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not appear to you like nothing in comparison?’
passages.sermon:
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the LORD spoke.
The LORD spoke through Haggai the prophet.
Haggai was a prophet.
The LORD gave Haggai a message.
The LORD told Haggai to speak to Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the son of Shealtiel.
Zerubbabel was the governor of Judah.
The LORD told Haggai to speak to Joshua.
Joshua was the son of Jehozadak.
Joshua was the high priest.
The LORD told Haggai to speak to the remnant of the people.
The LORD said, “Ask them this question.
Who among you is left who saw this house in its former glory?
How do you see it now?
Does it not seem to you like nothing in your eyes?”
passages.original: בַּשְּׁבִיעִ֕י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאֶחָ֖ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָה֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה בְּיַד־ חַגַּ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃ אֱמָר־ נָ֗א אֶל־ זְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בֶּן־ שַׁלְתִּיאֵל֙ פַּחַ֣ת יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בֶּן־ יְהוֹצָדָ֖ק הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֑וֹל וְאֶל־ שְׁאֵרִ֥ית הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ הַנִּשְׁאָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָאָה֙ אֶת־ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה בִּכְבוֹד֖וֹ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וּמָ֨ה אַתֶּ֜ם רֹאִ֤ים אֹתוֹ֙ עַ֔תָּה הֲל֥וֹא כָמֹ֛הוּ כְּאַ֖יִן בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But now be strong, O Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, O Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. And be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD. Work! For I am with you, declares the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the governor of Judah.
The LORD said, “Be strong, Zerubbabel.”
The LORD spoke to Joshua son of Jehozadak.
Joshua was the high priest.
The LORD said, “Be strong, Joshua.”
The LORD spoke to all the people of the land.
The LORD said, “Be strong, all you people.”
The LORD commanded, “Work!”
The LORD of Hosts said, “I am with you.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה חֲזַ֣ק זְרֻבָּבֶ֣ל׀ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֡ה וַחֲזַ֣ק יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בֶּן־ יְהוֹצָדָק֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וַחֲזַ֨ק כָּל־ עַ֥ם הָאָ֛רֶץ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֖ה וַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י אִתְּכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: This is the promise I made to you when you came out of Egypt. And My Spirit remains among you; do not be afraid.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God made a promise to them when they left Egypt.
God’s Spirit stays with them.
God tells them not to be afraid.
passages.original: אֶֽת־ הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־ כָּרַ֤תִּי אִתְּכֶם֙ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֣ם מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְרוּחִ֖י עֹמֶ֣דֶת בְּתוֹכְכֶ֑ם אַל־ תִּירָֽאוּ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts has all power.
The LORD of Hosts says this:
Soon, I will act again.
I will wait only a little while.
Then I will shake the heavens.
I will shake the earth.
I will shake the sea.
I will shake the dry land.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת ע֥וֹד אַחַ֖ת מְעַ֣ט הִ֑יא וַאֲנִ֗י מַרְעִישׁ֙ אֶת־ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶת־ הַיָּ֖ם וְאֶת־ הֶחָרָבָֽה׃

passages.text: I will shake all the nations, and they will come with all their treasures, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts has all power.
The LORD of Hosts will act.
The LORD of Hosts will shake all nations.
All nations will come.
They will bring their treasures.
The LORD of Hosts will fill this house with glory.
passages.original: וְהִרְעַשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבָ֖אוּ חֶמְדַּ֣ת כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמִלֵּאתִ֞י אֶת־ הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ כָּב֔וֹד אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, declares the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts is the God who commands all heavenly armies.
The LORD of Hosts says, “The silver belongs to Me.
The gold belongs to Me.”
passages.original: לִ֥י הַכֶּ֖סֶף וְלִ֣י הַזָּהָ֑ב נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of Hosts. And in this place I will provide peace, declares the LORD of Hosts.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is speaking.
The LORD of Hosts has all power and authority.
The LORD of Hosts says this about His house.
The glory of this house in the future will be greater than its glory in the past.
The LORD of Hosts promises this.
The LORD of Hosts will give peace in this place.
The LORD of Hosts declares this.
passages.original: גָּד֣וֹל יִֽהְיֶ֡ה כְּבוֹד֩ הַבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֤ה הָאַֽחֲרוֹן֙ מִן־ הָ֣רִאשׁ֔וֹן אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וּבַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן שָׁל֔וֹם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet, saying, “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Ask the priests for a ruling.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts spoke to Haggai the prophet.
This happened in the second year of King Darius.
It was the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month.
The LORD gave a message to Haggai.
The LORD said, “Ask the priests for a ruling.”
passages.original: בְּעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְאַרְבָּעָה֙ לַתְּשִׁיעִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָה֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ חַגַּ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת שְׁאַל־ נָ֧א אֶת־ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים תּוֹרָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

passages.text: If a man carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and it touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any other food, does that item become holy?’ ” “No,” replied the priests.
passages.sermon:
Haggai was a prophet of the LORD.
The LORD of Hosts spoke to Haggai.
The LORD told Haggai to ask the priests a question.
A man carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment.
The fold of his garment touches bread.
The fold touches stew.
The fold touches wine.
The fold touches oil.
The fold touches any other food.
Haggai asked the priests, “Does the food become holy?”
The priests answered, “No.”
passages.original: הֵ֣ן׀ יִשָּׂא־ אִ֨ישׁ בְּשַׂר־ קֹ֜דֶשׁ בִּכְנַ֣ף בִּגְד֗וֹ וְנָגַ֣ע בִּ֠כְנָפוֹ אֶל־ הַלֶּ֨חֶם וְאֶל־ הַנָּזִ֜יד וְאֶל־ הַיַּ֧יִן וְאֶל־ שֶׁ֛מֶן וְאֶל־ כָּל־ מַאֲכָ֖ל הֲיִקְדָּ֑שׁ וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹֽא׃

passages.text: So Haggai asked, “If one who is defiled by contact with a corpse touches any of these, does it become defiled?” “Yes, it becomes defiled,” the priests answered.
passages.sermon:
Haggai was a prophet of the LORD.
Haggai spoke to the priests.
Haggai asked a question about ritual purity.
He said, "If a person is defiled by contact with a corpse, and he touches any of these foods, does the food become defiled?"
The priests answered Haggai.
They said, "Yes, it becomes defiled."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חַגַּ֔י אִם־ יִגַּ֧ע טְמֵא־ נֶ֛פֶשׁ בְּכָל־ אֵ֖לֶּה הֲיִטְמָ֑א וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יִטְמָֽא׃

passages.text: Then Haggai replied, “So it is with this people and this nation before Me, declares the LORD, and so it is with every work of their hands; whatever they offer there is defiled.
passages.sermon:
Haggai spoke to the people.
He said, “This people is unclean before the LORD.
This nation is also unclean before the LORD.
The LORD declares this.
Everything they do is unclean.
Every work of their hands is unclean.
Whatever they offer at the altar is unclean.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן חַגַּ֜י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֵּ֣ן הָֽעָם־ הַ֠זֶּה וְכֵן־ הַגּ֨וֹי הַזֶּ֤ה לְפָנַי֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְכֵ֖ן כָּל־ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיהֶ֑ם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יַקְרִ֛יבוּ שָׁ֖ם טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Now consider carefully from this day forward: Before one stone was placed on another in the temple of the LORD, from that time, when one came expecting a heap of twenty ephahs of grain, there were but ten. When one came to the winepress to draw out fifty baths, there were but twenty.
passages.sermon:
Haggai was a prophet of the LORD.
He spoke to the people of Judah.
He told them to think carefully about their lives.
He said, “Start from this day and look forward.”
He reminded them about the time before they rebuilt the LORD’s temple.
He said, “Before you placed one stone on another in the LORD’s temple, things were hard.”
He gave examples.
He said, “When someone came to a pile of grain expecting twenty measures, there were only ten.”
He said, “When someone came to the winepress to draw out fifty measures, there were only twenty.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ שִֽׂימוּ־ נָ֣א לְבַבְכֶ֔ם מִן־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה מִטֶּ֧רֶם שֽׂוּם־ אֶ֛בֶן אֶל־ אֶ֖בֶן בְּהֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃ מִֽהְיוֹתָ֥ם בָּא֙ אֶל־ עֲרֵמַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְהָיְתָ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֑ה בָּ֣א אֶל־ הַיֶּ֗קֶב לַחְשֹׂף֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים פּוּרָ֔ה וְהָיְתָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִֽים׃

passages.text: I struck you—all the work of your hands—with blight, mildew, and hail, but you did not turn to Me, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the people of Israel.
The LORD said, "I struck you with blight.
I struck you with mildew.
I struck you with hail.
I struck all the work of your hands.
But you did not turn to Me."
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: הִכֵּ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בַּשִּׁדָּפ֤וֹן וּבַיֵּֽרָקוֹן֙ וּבַבָּרָ֔ד אֵ֖ת כָּל־ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיכֶ֑ם וְאֵין־ אֶתְכֶ֥ם אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Consider carefully from this day forward—from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid—consider carefully: Is there still seed in the barn? The vine, the fig, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yet yielded fruit. But from this day on, I will bless you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the people of Judah through Haggai.
The LORD told them to pay close attention.
He said, “Think carefully from this day forward.
Today is the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month.
This is the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid.
Consider this day carefully.
Ask yourselves: Is there still seed left in the barn?
The vine has not produced fruit.
The fig tree has not produced fruit.
The pomegranate tree has not produced fruit.
The olive tree has not produced fruit.
But from this day on, I will bless you.”
passages.original: שִׂימוּ־ נָ֣א לְבַבְכֶ֔ם מִן־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה מִיּוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לַתְּשִׁיעִ֗י לְמִן־ הַיּ֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יֻסַּ֥ד הֵֽיכַל־ יְהוָ֖ה שִׂ֥ימוּ לְבַבְכֶֽם׃ הַע֤וֹד הַזֶּ֙רַע֙ בַּמְּגוּרָ֔ה וְעַד־ הַגֶּ֨פֶן וְהַתְּאֵנָ֧ה וְהָרִמּ֛וֹן וְעֵ֥ץ הַזַּ֖יִת לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֑א מִן־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲבָרֵֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: For the second time that day, the twenty-fourth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to Haggai, saying, “Tell Zerubbabel governor of Judah that I am about to shake the heavens and the earth: I will overturn royal thrones and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month.
The LORD gave Haggai a message.
The LORD told Haggai to speak to Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the governor of Judah.
The LORD said, “I am about to shake the heavens and the earth.
I will overturn royal thrones.
I will destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations.
I will overturn chariots and their riders.
Horses and their riders will fall.
Each man will fall by the sword of his brother.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֤ה׀ שֵׁנִית֙ אֶל־ חַגַּ֔י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֛ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר׃ אֱמֹ֕ר אֶל־ זְרֻבָּבֶ֥ל פַּֽחַת־ יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֲנִ֣י מַרְעִ֔ישׁ אֶת־ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃ וְהָֽפַכְתִּי֙ כִּסֵּ֣א מַמְלָכ֔וֹת וְהִ֨שְׁמַדְתִּ֔י חֹ֖זֶק מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְהָפַכְתִּ֤י מֶרְכָּבָה֙ וְרֹ֣כְבֶ֔יהָ וְיָרְד֤וּ סוּסִים֙ וְרֹ֣כְבֵיהֶ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ בְּחֶ֥רֶב אָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: On that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, I will take you, My servant, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, declares the LORD, and I will make you like My signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of Hosts.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He speaks about a special day.
He addresses Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel is the son of Shealtiel.
Zerubbabel serves the LORD.
The LORD says, “I will take you, Zerubbabel.”
The LORD says, “I will make you like my signet ring.”
A signet ring shows authority and approval.
The LORD says, “I have chosen you, Zerubbabel.”
The LORD of Hosts declares this.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֣וּא נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֡וֹת אֶ֠קָּחֲךָ זְרֻבָּבֶ֨ל בֶּן־ שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵ֤ל עַבְדִּי֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךָ כַּֽחוֹתָ֑ם כִּֽי־ בְךָ֣ בָחַ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
